claims.summary: The article gives an April 11–May 18 Iowa corn advisory window, while emphasizing soil conditions over fixed dates.

spatial_support.description: Iowa statewide extension guidance; Story County is a pilot within this scope.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: Historical 2021 guidance, not a planting authorization or insurance calendar. No cultivar-specific or Story County trial dates are supplied.

claims.locator: Paragraph on planting corn versus soybean, before May 20
claims.summary: The article favors soybean planting before May 20 when conditions permit. No universal earliest date is extracted.

spatial_support.description: Iowa extension guidance; no farm-level planting observation.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: Earlier insurance dates in this article are policy dates, not crop requirements. This advisory endpoint is not a hard biological limit.

claims.locator: Why Soil Temperatures Matter; Soil temperature trend
claims.summary: For corn and soybean establishment, the article favors soil above 50°F with a warming 3–7 day outlook.

spatial_support.description: Iowa extension guidance, variable field conditions.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: This is soil-temperature establishment guidance, never monthly air-temperature tolerance. The advice does not specify one universal measurement depth; referenced 4-inch maps do not establish field seed-zone temperature. No forecast was retrieved.

claims.summary: The article advises a seedbed that crumbles rather than smears and checking for wet soil below a dry surface.

spatial_support.description: Iowa regional seedbed guidance, requiring local inspection.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: Qualitative seedbed fitness is not a numeric moisture, texture, drainage class or soil-depth threshold.

claims.locator: Early planting considerations, warm soil paragraph
claims.summary: Early soybean planting calls for warm soil that does not cool during the first 24 hours.

spatial_support.description: Iowa extension guidance for early soybean establishment.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: No safe-forecast conclusion can be drawn without a current relevant forecast and field conditions.

claims.summary: Soybean germination at 50°F is discussed at a two-inch soil depth, conditional on seedbed quality.

spatial_support.description: Iowa statewide guidance; stated measurement depth, not a soil sampling horizon.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: Two inches converts exactly to 5.08 cm. This is a temperature reference depth, not a required root-zone depth or soil-property layer. It must not be used for a soil-depth compatibility rule.

claims.summary: No-till wheat–sorghum–fallow was among rotations researched near Tribune. The listing does not prescribe a farm rotation.

spatial_support.description: K-State Southwest Research-Extension Center near Tribune, Kansas; not every field in Greeley County.

temporal_support.description: Published research interval; endpoint days denote year extent, not individual observation dates.

limitations: The abstract is a research summary. No numerical crop requirements, calendar, yield projection or transferable rotation benefit is extracted.

claims.locator: Keys to Water Management Success, printed p.119 / PDF p.18; AWD sections pp.114–120
claims.summary: Flooded rice requires managed water delivery, retention and drainage. The chapter distinguishes conventional flood, AWD and cultivar-related exceptions.

spatial_support.description: Arkansas flooded-rice production guidance, not a Stuttgart field observation.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: Management depends on cultivar, growth stage, soil and irrigation capacity. Numerical flood depth and timing were not promoted to universal requirements. Rainfall is not an irrigation-sufficiency measurement.

claims.summary: The handbook emphasizes surface drainage for irrigated soybean.

spatial_support.description: Arkansas irrigated soybean guidance; no Stuttgart-specific soil sampling.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: This is an old (2000) chapter and remains reference-only. No numeric water, soil or yield rule is extracted; current local review is needed.

claims.summary: Drill-sown rice is established with flush irrigation before permanent water, with timing dependent on crop stage.

spatial_support.description: Southern NSW rice-management reference for the Riverina pilot; no Griffith field-specific evidence.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: Only the landing-page summary was audited. Full guide, variety calendar, irrigation allocation and soil suitability remain unverified; no aerial-sowing inference is permitted.

claims.locator: Crop coefficient approach, equation 56 and units
claims.summary: Standard-condition crop evapotranspiration equals stage-specific Kc times reference ET0. Both ET rates use mm/day and Kc is dimensionless.

spatial_support.description: General method under the documented standard conditions; not a regional crop coefficient.

temporal_support.description: Publication guidance, not a dated field observation; original study dates unavailable.

limitations: No crop-specific coefficients were ingested. Monthly mean air temperature and rainfall alone do not supply ET0 or a complete field water balance. Flooded rice also needs separate water-management terms.
